sources.title: Sailer, Hense, Mayr & Mandl (2017): How gamification motivates
sources.access: author-uploaded article text, abstract and discussion reviewed
sources.finding: Different configurations of game elements affected different reported needs; perceived decision freedom was not changed as intended.
sources.designInference: Treat game elements individually and do not promise that points make a worldview questionnaire fun or valid.

sources.title: Pölzler (2018): How to Measure Moral Realism
sources.access: full HTML available; abstract and sections 1–7 reviewed
sources.finding: Related philosophical positions, incomplete answer choices and first-order moral prompts can undermine intended construct measurement.
sources.designInference: Preserve question wording and distinctions; avoid ideology targets or congratulating particular answers while answering.

sources.title: W3C: Understanding Target Size (Minimum)
sources.designInference: Large controls, adequate spacing, keyboard access and no drag-only rankings.

sources.title: W3C: Understanding Animation from Interactions
sources.designInference: Respect reduced-motion preferences and do not require animation or sound.

evidenceLimit: The UI is designed for enjoyment. Enjoyment, completion gains and psychological measurement equivalence have not been demonstrated with participants. Deterministic code tests establish software noninterference only.
routeLengthMeaning: Assigned distinct items; inapplicable conditional follow-ups are skipped and recorded separately. The 240-item route is not the entire master bank.
